headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear the costs of new grid infrastructure and capacity increases necessitated by their high demand, thereby protecting residential ratepayers from these expenses.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Dominion Energy, Governor's administration, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Shifts Electricity Costs to Data Centers, Cuts Residential Bills
news_summary: A Virginia bill aims to shift electricity costs for grid upgrades and capacity from residential customers to large users like data centers, potentially decreasing average residential bills by over 3%. Dominion Energy supports this legislation, stating it ensures data centers pay their fair share and lowers costs for other customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This legislation requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency and enabling better management of Virginia's water resources.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental advocacy groups (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters), local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed SB 553, requiring water utilities to report monthly water consumption by data centers to the State Water Control Board. This aims to address concerns about the industry's significant water usage and provide crucial data for resource planning, especially as Virginia hosts the world's largest concentration of data centers.

headline: Local Data Center Siting, Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill empowers Virginia localities to require site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to study noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and to consider other environmental and infrastructure impacts before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, local government associations, environmental and conservation groups (e.g., Virginia Farm Bureau, Virginia Forestry Association, Virginia Conservation Network, Piedmont Environmental Council, National Parks Conservation Association), Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Senator Danica A. Roem.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law: What It Does and Doesn't Do
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers (100 MW+) to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools before local approval. While it mandates studies and utility disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some regulatory power to localities.
